messages:
maya: Heads-up — we need to decide how telemetry ingest should degrade when worker SLOs hit pressure. Thinking SLO-prioritized shedding using a bandit-style priority per-tenant. Tradeoffs?
kevin: +1. Do you mean a multi-armed bandit that updates sampling probs per-tenant based on a reward signal?
maya: Yes. Reward = downstream correctness/latency (lower is better), cost = ingest tokens. Update probs every minute or hour depending on traffic.
tom: Concern: exploration noise could cause oscillation and cascading reconfig churn. Need smoothing/decay + safety floors per tier.
maya: Agreed. My rough plan: epsilon-greedy with annealing + min_quota for paid tiers and a tiny head-sample for debugging.
kevin: Also we must avoid observability blind spots. Keep deterministic head samples for error-prone routes and a small global head_sample.
maya: config prototype (staging):
```
ingest_shedder:
  mode: epsilon_greedy
  epsilon_start: 0.2
  epsilon_min: 0.02
  decay_days: 7
  min_quota:
    enterprise: 0.1
    standard: 0.02
  head_sample_rate: 0.001
```

tom: Ops implications: where to store bandit weights? Prefer a consistent-hash + small Redis cluster or a raft-backed kv. Need fast reads in the router path. How do we bootstrap weights after deploys?
maya: Bootstrap plan: persist weights with TTL, on deploy decay weights toward uniform over 24h and emit an audit event. Policy versions checked into git for reproducibility.
ops-bot: deploy-gate: reminder — rollout must include kill-switch and circuit-breaker in router. Use feature-flag + manual override. :white_check_mark:
kevin: Metrics to emit: sampled_rate_by_tenant, shedder_reward, incoming_drop_rate, downstream_error_rate, restore_time_seconds. Also histogram of per-tenant latency shift post-shed.
maya: Open question: per-route bandit vs global per-tenant. Per-route is higher fidelity but much higher cardinality/cost.
tom: Tradeoff: start global per-tenant for most tenants, escalate to per-route for top N hot tenants. Add sharding cap to bound state.
maya: Action items: A) prototype epsilon-greedy shedder in staging (kevin) B) infra design for weight store + circuit breaker (tom) C) eval hooks + dashboards + alerts (maya) D) canary: 1% traffic, rollbackable.
kevin: I'll open an RFC follow-up PR with simulation harness and config defaults, include toy sim results (bandit vs fixed-rate sampling).
maya: thanks. linking simulation doc: https://redwood.internal/sim/shedder-bandit-v1 :eyes: 
tom: If we see oscillation in sim or staging, fallback to simple rate-limiter per-tenant and increase head_sample_rate for debugging.
maya: Ack. :thumbsup:
